difficulty.reason: Self-serve internal install with app manifests; review only required for the public Slack App Directory.

timeEstimate.approvalWait: Instant for private workspaces; 2 - 4 weeks for public App Directory
timeEstimate.notes: Developers can immediately install and test in development workspaces without waiting for Slack approval.

requirements: A Slack workspace where you have admin or app creation permissions
HTTPS redirect URL (or localhost for development)
Valid privacy policy URL (if distributing publicly)
App icon (512x512 PNG) and short description

steps.title: Create an App via Manifest or Scratch
steps.description: Go to api.slack.com/apps and click 'Create New App'. Selecting 'From an app manifest' allows pasting a YAML/JSON file with all permissions pre-configured.

steps.title: Configure OAuth Redirect URLs & Scopes
steps.description: Under 'OAuth & Permissions', add your redirect URL. Select Bot Token Scopes (e.g. chat:write, channels:read, users:read) based on the actions your agent will perform.

steps.title: Install to Workspace for Immediate Testing
steps.description: Click 'Install to Workspace' in the sidebar. Confirm permissions to generate a Bot User OAuth Token (`xoxb-...`) that can be used immediately.

steps.title: Activate Public Distribution (Optional)
steps.description: If external users will connect their own workspaces via OAuth, enable Public Distribution under 'Manage Distribution' and verify that all landing page URLs are live.

blockers.problem: Workspace administrator restricts non-approved third-party apps
blockers.solution: Submit an in-workspace request to the Slack admin, or create a free personal Slack workspace for staging and development.

blockers.problem: Redirect URI mismatch error during OAuth code exchange
blockers.solution: Verify that the redirect URL in your authorization request matches character-for-character the URL whitelisted under OAuth & Permissions.

blockers.problem: Scope escalation invalidates previous user tokens
blockers.solution: When adding new scopes, prompt existing users to re-authorize before making API calls with newly requested capabilities.

agentCanDo: Generate the complete Slack App Manifest (YAML/JSON) with required scopes and events
Implement the OAuth 2.0 exchange route and token storage
Handle Slack event subscriptions and URL verification challenges (`url_verification`)
developerMustDo: Log in to api.slack.com and create the application
Authorize the installation in the target Slack workspace
Copy Client ID and Client Secret into the environment variables (`.env`)
Submit for App Directory review if building a multi-tenant public product

managedOption.managedSufficientWhen: Using Composio or a managed OAuth provider is sufficient when building an internal AI agent or multi-tenant app where users connect their individual Slack workspaces via standard OAuth.
managedOption.customRequiredWhen: You must register a custom Slack OAuth app if you require bespoke bot branding (custom name/avatar in Slack channels), enterprise Grid approval, or private slash commands.

claims.claim: Apps do not need Slack review or approval to be installed on development or private workspaces.
Public distribution requires submitting a privacy policy, support URL, and passing Slack App Directory review.
Granular bot scopes are strictly enforced and cannot be changed dynamically per authorization.

openQuestions: How frequently does Slack audit enterprise workspace apps that use wide conversation history scopes without listing on the App Directory?
